disassembly.observation: Exact instruction stream for offsets, constants, strides, call shapes and the bare RET return form.

observed_mechanics: 0x006a2a80..0x006a2a83: PUSH EBX; PUSH EBP; PUSH ESI; MOV EBX,ECX - the receiver arrives in ECX and is kept in EBX.
0x006a2a85: MOV EBP,dword ptr [EBX + 0x18] - the begin cursor of the entry range is read into EBP.
0x006a2a89: MOV EDI,dword ptr [EBX + 0x1c] - the end cursor of the entry range is read into EDI.
0x006a2a8c: LEA ESI,[EBX + 0x18] - ESI is formed as receiver+0x18 and is reused both as the second call's receiver and as the base for the [ESI+0x4] store, so [ESI+0x4] is receiver+0x1c.

0x006a2a8f..0x006a2a92: PUSH EBP; PUSH EDI; PUSH EDI; CALL 0x00612b20 - the pushed range is degenerate because the first two words are the same register, so the helper's loop pretest fails and its third argument is returned in EAX.
0x006a2a97: MOV ECX,dword ptr [ESI + 0x4] - the end cursor is re-read from memory after the first call, not taken from the stale register.
0x006a2a9a: ADD ESP,0xc - the caller, not the callee, removes the three words of the first call.

0x006a2a9d..0x006a2aa1: PUSH ECX; PUSH EAX; MOV ECX,ESI; CALL 0x00685a30 - the release helper receives receiver+0x18 as its thiscall receiver, the first call's result as its first word, and the re-read end cursor as its second word.
0x006a2aa6: SUB EDI,EBP - the span is a byte subtraction of the two cursors captured before the calls, not an element count.
0x006a2aa8..0x006a2aad: MOV EAX,0xd5555555; IMUL EDI - a signed 32x32 multiply whose high half lands in EDX.
0x006a2aaf..0x006a2ab7: SAR EDX,0x2; MOV EAX,EDX; SHR EAX,0x1f; ADD EAX,EDX - arithmetic shift by two followed by a sign-bit correction, i.e. a truncating division of the span by the element stride.

0x006a2ab9..0x006a2ac1: LEA EDX,[EAX + EAX*2] then ADD EDX,EDX three times - the corrected quotient is scaled by three and then by eight, giving the product of the quotient and the 0x18 element stride.

0x006a2ac3: ADD dword ptr [ESI + 0x4],EDX - the product is added to the word at that displacement as it stands at this instruction, so for a span that is a whole number of strides the end cursor is rewound onto the begin cursor and the range is emptied. The candidate re-reads the word at this point rather than reusing the pre-call register copy, so its store does not depend on the release helper having left the word unchanged.
0x006a2ac6: INC dword ptr [EBX + 0x34] - a counter word at receiver+0x34 is incremented unconditionally after the store.
0x006a2ac9..0x006a2acc: POP ESI; POP EBP; POP EBX; RET - a bare RET with no stack cleanup, confirming a thiscall with no explicit stack arguments.

observed_original_abi.reason: The contract below is the persisted ABI record for this target (categories.abi, evidence_level SUPPORTED), corroborated by the machine body: ECX is copied to EBX by the third instruction, no argument word is ever read from the stack, and the epilogue is a bare RET with no immediate.

flow: Read the begin cursor from receiver+0x18 and the end cursor from receiver+0x1c.
Call 0x00612b20 with the degenerate range (end, end, begin); the helper returns the begin cursor.
Call 0x00685a30 with receiver+0x18 as receiver, the returned cursor as first word, and the re-read end cursor as second word.
Compute trunc((end - begin) / 0x18) via the 0xd5555555 multiply-shift sequence and add the result times 0x18 to the end cursor.
Increment the counter word at receiver+0x34.

observed_state_contract.span_subtraction: byte subtraction of the two cursors, taken from registers loaded before either call, not from the re-read memory word
state_writes: receiver+0x1c (end cursor) via ADD dword ptr [ESI + 0x4],EDX
state_reads: receiver+0x1c (end cursor), read twice: once at 0x006a2a89 into EDI and once at 0x006a2a97 into ECX

unresolved_questions: The identity of the receiver words at 0x18, 0x1c and 0x34. The machine-derived receiver record is bounds_only and enumerates displacements, not members, so the candidate deliberately names none. A struct layout naming these words requires a source outside this body (the SDK header, or a writer elsewhere in the binary that documents them).

The general (non-degenerate) arm of 0x00612b20, now read but not ported: per element it writes the dword at +0x00 inline and thiscall-calls 0x00542b80 with ECX = out_element+0x4 and the source's +0x4 pushed, so each 0x18 entry is a four-dword block plus two flag words copied with flag-dependent side effects rather than a flat memcpy. Only the degenerate return observed at this call site is claimed here.

What 0x0093db80, the release target 0x00685a30 selects with `TEST byte ptr [ESI + 0x14],0x4` on each entry, actually does. Its body tests `byte ptr [ESI + 0x10],0x4` on the address it is handed, and when that is set it makes an indirect call through the data word at 0x0154eb48 with six pushed words. That indirect target is outside this record's scope and is not claimed.

The concrete layout of the 0x18 entry. What is observable from the two callees is a dword at +0x00 and a sub-object at +0x04 spanning to the 0x18 stride boundary, carrying a flag word at its +0x10 and a count word at its +0x12. That is a callee-derived shape, not a claim about 0x006a2a80, and the candidate still declares the element type incomplete.

Whether the byte span at receiver+0x18..0x1c is always an exact multiple of the 0x18 stride. The rewind only lands on the begin cursor when it is; for a ragged span the end cursor is rewound to the nearest lower stride boundary.
Identity and initial value of the counter word at receiver+0x34 and its readers elsewhere in the binary.
The concrete layout of the receiver between offsets 0x00 and 0x17 and between 0x20 and 0x33, which this body never touches.

Whether the shared vtable 0x01408820 dispatches this body at a fixed slot, and which callers reach it. The single xref is the vtable word at 0x01408868; no direct caller exists in the xref export, so reachability is dispatch mediated and stays a runtime gate.
